rules.title: Statewide rent control ballot initiative (Initiative Petition 25-21) blocked by SJC
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide cap limiting annual rent increases to the lesser of CPI or 5% will not appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law and no statewide cap applies.
rules.requirement_es: Una propuesta de límite estatal que limitaría los aumentos anuales de alquiler al menor entre el IPC o el 5% no aparecerá en la boleta de noviembre de 2026; no es ley y no se aplica ningún límite estatal.
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.key_value: Lesser of CPI increase or 5% (proposed only)
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units; exemptions for owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.caveat: Secondary source (law firm blog). Initiative was blocked by the SJC in Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893, because of its religious-purpose exemption; proponents may re-file.

no_rule_findings.finding: No rent cap: existing Massachusetts statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P) remains in place after the SJC kept the repeal initiative off the ballot.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases

no_rule_findings.finding: No rent cap: state law bars local rent control.
